Start the interactive LOGOS REPL.

Two modes in one session: imperative statements against a persistent interpreter session (`logos>`), and English→FOL logic mode with discourse-aware anaphora (`logic>`). Type `:help` inside for the meta-commands (`:mode`, `:format`, `:readings`, `:vars`, `:save`, …). Works on a pipe too — no terminal required.

Usage: largo repl [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --logic
          Start in logic mode (English → FOL)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Initial logic output format

          Possible values:
          - unicode: Unicode logic symbols: ∀, ∃, ∧, ∨, ¬, →
          - latex:   LaTeX markup: \forall, \exists, \land, ...
          - ascii:   Plain ASCII FOL
          - kripke:  Kripke semantics: modals lowered to explicit world quantification

      --load <LOAD>
          Load a saved session/program on startup

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo repl
  largo repl --logic
  largo repl --logic --format latex
  largo repl --load session.lg
  printf 'Let x be 5.\nShow x.\n' | largo repl
